claim_scope: nominal dynamics, latency, and observation parameters can produce a measurable held-out rollout gap
observation-only calibration exposes two zero-error gain/scale minimizers and remains ambiguous on a separate action sequence
adding an independent state anchor selects one target grid candidate in the deterministic fixture
domain-randomization coverage depends on whether the target parameter vector lies inside the declared support
repeating one known-load condition preserves three force/load-equivalent grid points, while a second distinct known load selects one target candidate in the deterministic fixture

code.config: standard-library scalar actuator, delay, observation-scale, and known-load multi-condition calibration fixture

data.name: procedural calibration and held-out action sequences

limitations: one-dimensional deterministic dynamics rather than rigid-body/contact simulation
target parameters and one observation-equivalent alternative are contained in a small hand-authored calibration grid
zero held-out error is a fixture property and not expected for real system identification
no images, contacts, stochasticity, continuous optimization, policy learning, simulator, hardware, vehicle, or GPU
state anchor is directly available in the fixture and does not establish which measurements are available on a real system
known payload values are exact and the two-condition unique solution is specific to a noiseless nine-point grid, not a general identifiability guarantee
